inputs.share_count_basis: 131,489,535 issued less 731,098 treasury at 2026-06-30 (Q1 FY2027 tanshin) = 130.76m. Held FLAT. The JPY70bn zero-coupon convertibles issued 2026-07-24 (JPY35bn due 2030 at JPY5,275; JPY35bn due 2032 at JPY5,105) are OUT of the money at the current price and are carried as debt; if both converted they would add ~13.5m shares (+10%) and remove JPY70bn of debt -- roughly value-neutral per share at an IV near the conversion prices, dilutive above them.
inputs.net_debt_note: Q1 FY2027 balance sheet (2026-06-30): short-term borrowings 330,518 + commercial paper 100,000 + current bonds 10,000 + bonds 110,000 + long-term borrowings 154,387 = 704,905; cash and deposits 157,006. Matches the company's own net interest-bearing debt definition (net D/E ~0.71x). EXCLUDED, deliberately: the gold-bullion lease/deposit book (leased gold bullion asset 772bn vs deposited gold bullion liability 1,097bn) which is gold-denominated funding of in-process smelter inventory, not financial debt, and the JPY38.7bn retirement benefit liability (service cost already inside operating profit). The July-2026 convertibles post-date this balance sheet; their proceeds are cash, so net debt is unchanged at issuance.
inputs.reported_fcf_note: FY2026 OCF 39,674 less capex 54,982 (Integrated Report 2026 eleven-year summary). Reported OCF is noisy: gold-bullion sale/lease flows and metal-price-driven working capital swing it by tens of billions a year. The forward build is from components, not from this anchor.
inputs.interest_income_note: FY2026 interest income ~JPY3.5-4bn is left inside the flows: the company is a net DEBTOR (net debt 548bn), so the interest-income strip rule (net cash > 1x FCF base) does not apply.
inputs.sbc_source: No share-based payment line in the J-GAAP cash flow statement; the only equity-settled remuneration is a restricted-stock element of director pay (Integrated Report 2026, governance section), immaterial. SBC-zero market: sbc = 0, rows kept explicit at 0%, house and street coincide.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 treasury purchases JPY20m (odd-lot buybacks only). FY2026 Q1 FY2027: treasury shares fell 812k -> 731k (restricted-stock delivery). Flat count is a modelling convention the company funds via dividends (JPY116/share FY2027 forecast, DOE 2.5%), not buybacks.
inputs.wacc_rationale: JPY-built. Risk-free 10y JGB ~1.7%, Japan ERP 6.0%, beta ~1.3 for a copper/gold/tungsten-linked smelter -> cost of equity ~9.5%. Pre-tax cost of debt ~1.5% (FY2026 interest paid ~JPY9-10bn on ~650bn gross), ~1.0% after tax. Weighted at the company's TARGET structure (net D/E 0.5x, ~33% debt) rather than today's cycle-depressed market cap (49% debt), which would give ~5.3%: 0.67 x 9.5 + 0.33 x 1.0 = 6.8%, rounded to 7.0%. No ad-hoc cyclicality premium: cyclicality is charged once, in the mid-cycle fade and the scenario weights. Same WACC in all three scenarios.
inputs.lease_treatment: J-GAAP filer: operating leases are expensed inside operating profit and no lease liabilities are carried on the balance sheet. No adjustment -- leases are neither deducted from the flows a second time nor added to net debt.
inputs.nci_treatment: Consolidated flows; non-controlling interests deducted once in the equity bridge at book (JPY17,590m at 2026-06-30, ~2.2% of net assets). NCI fell from 32bn (FY2024) to 16-18bn after the aluminium and other divestitures, so historical NCI dividends (7.5-13.5bn/yr) overstate forward leakage.
inputs.ebitda_definition: Adjusted EBITDA = operating profit + dividend income + share of profit of equity-method affiliates + D&A, i.e. ordinary profit before net interest and FX, plus D&A. The mine stakes (Los Pelambres dividends, Mantoverde equity income) and, from ~Feb 2027, the ~32% equity-method stake in Pan Pacific Copper are core to the business, so their income is kept IN the flows and the matching assets (investment securities JPY302bn at 2026-06-30, mostly these stakes at carrying value) are NOT added to the bridge. Calibration: FY2026 = 60.5 + 23.4 + 21.2 + 49.9 = JPY155.0bn = 8.4% of revenue; FY2025 = 37.1 + 20.1 + 17.5 + 47.3 = 122bn = 6.2%; FY2027 guidance = 130 + 37.3 + 30.0 + ~47 = 244bn = 10.2% (10.0% ex the +3.5bn inventory-valuation gain). Ten-year average ~8%.
inputs.cash_tax_note: 23% blended cash rate on pre-interest EBIT: ~31% statutory on the operating component, ~0% on foreign-affiliate dividends (95% exempt) and on equity-method income (already post-tax), which are ~35-40% of ordinary profit going forward. Cross-check: FY2027 guidance pre-tax ~184bn -> net 140bn + NCI implies ~23%; FY2022/FY2024 cash taxes paid were 21% of ordinary profit.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF component DCF (operating company, non-US cyclical -- SKILL.md row 2, owner-fcf.md plus owner-fcf-adaptations.md). Fresh build, no prior DCF. Reporting currency JPY = quote currency JPY, no FX bridge. THE CENTRAL JUDGMENT IS MID-CYCLE NORMALISATION: FY2027 guidance (ordinary profit JPY180bn, net JPY140bn, ROE 18.5%) rests on APT tungsten at $3,017/MTU vs $855 a year earlier, gold $4,129, copper 579c and JPY158/$, plus a low-cost tungsten inventory release management says fades from Q4; management's own FY2029 targets (ROE 8%+, ROIC 7%+) imply net profit ~JPY70-75bn and ordinary ~JPY100-105bn. Year 1 is taken at guidance (Q1 already delivered 51.9bn ordinary); years 2-3 fade to that management-defined mid-cycle; the terminal margin (7.8%) sits just below the ten-year average on a higher price-deck revenue base. The Pan Pacific Copper company split (~Feb 2027) will remove an undisclosed but large slice of cathode-sales revenue and move the profit into equity-method income; it is NOT modelled as a revenue drop (a negative WC capture on a deconsolidation would book a phantom cash release) -- revenue falls only for metal-price normalisation, and the later-year margins are on a pre-split revenue basis to be re-based when FY2028 is restated. The market cap (JPY567bn) is roughly equal to net debt: equity is a levered call on the metals cycle, which is why the bear case lands near zero.

equity_bridge.note: Q1 FY2027 tanshin balance sheet, 2026-06-30. Deducted once; flows are consolidated.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: long-run revenue growth 1.5-2% after a price-driven FY2027 spike and FY2028-29 normalisation; equity CAGR (7.5-7.8%) is retained earnings on a 5% ROE base, not a growth signal
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: EPS 3yr CAGR negative (FY2023 base 155.6 -> FY2026 310.6 is +25.9%/yr; FY2022 base 344.6 -> FY2026 is -2.6%/yr) and 5yr undefined (FY2021 base follows the FY2020 loss) -- commodity earnings have no stable trend. Owner-FCF CAGRs undefined: FY2022-26 owner FCF was negative in four of five years (reported FCF -64.6, -25.6, -27.4, +2.8, -15.3bn).
historical_growth.notes: Revenue FY2023->FY2026 1,625.9 -> 1,844.1 (+4.3%/yr); FY2021->FY2026 1,485.1 -> 1,844.1 (+4.4%/yr -- 4.0% quoted on the FY2021 ASBJ-29 restated basis). Equity (parent) FY2023 593.3 -> FY2026 736.1 (+7.5%/yr); FY2021 545.2 -> 736.1 (+6.2%/yr before the FY2026 OCI jump; 7.8% incl.). Cumulative company-defined FCF FY2016-FY2026 ~JPY110bn over eleven years (~10bn/yr), which is the single most important historical fact for this valuation.

base.growth_note: Y1 = FY2027 guidance JPY2,400bn (+30.1%). Y2-3 give back part of the price deck (copper 579c, gold 4,129, APT 3,017) and the JPY158/$ assumption; thereafter 1.5-2% nominal JPY growth. The PPC deconsolidation is not in the revenue path (see inputs.notes).
base.margin_note: Y1 10.0% = FY2027 guidance ex inventory gain (OP 126.5 + div 37.3 + eq 30.0 + D&A 47 on 2,400). Y2 8.5% (~ordinary 130bn: tungsten inventory tailwind gone, PPC equity income in). Y3 7.6% = management's FY2029 mid-cycle (ordinary ~105bn, ROE 8%). Terminal 7.8%, just under the ten-year average of ~8%.
base.capex_note: FY2027 cash-basis capex guided ~JPY80bn (construction basis 94bn) on secondary-smelter / recycling growth projects; FY2016-2024 ran 76-103bn, FY2025-26 55-59bn. Terminal 3.0% of revenue (~JPY70bn) vs D&A 2.4% (~JPY58bn): growth capex persists under the resource-circulation strategy.
base.wc_note: Manufacturer with receivables + inventory >> payables, so capture is NEGATIVE: metal-price-driven revenue growth consumes cash. -15% x FY2027 revenue increase of 556bn = -83bn vs the company's guided -107bn working-capital outflow; the FY2028-29 revenue give-back releases ~35bn, consistent with inventories unwinding at lower prices.
base.terminal_note: Cap 12x terminal-year FCF (cyclical, structurally low-return industry: ROIC 4-6% FY2024-26). Gordon at 7%/1% would be ~16.8x; the cap binds.

bull.margin_note: Price deck holds (copper >550c on the electrification/AI-datacentre deficit, gold >4,000, tungsten export controls keep APT elevated, yen stays weak); PPC consolidation lifts smelting returns; Onahama exit and plant integrations deliver; FY2029 targets beaten (ordinary ~150bn sustained = 9% EBITDA margin, ROE ~12%).

bear.margin_note: FY2027 misses the raised guidance (H2 tungsten/gold roll over, yen firms to ~145); FY2028-29 revert to the FY2024-25 earnings band (ordinary 55-65bn, EBITDA margin 6.2-6.5%, the FY2024 level was 7.2% and FY2025 6.2%); TC/RC stays at historic lows; growth capex continues at 3.5% of revenue with the recycling build-out; another restructuring impairment cycle. Equity is a thin residual over 548bn of net debt.

scenario_narratives.base: FY2027 lands at the August guidance (Q1 already delivered JPY51.9bn of the JPY180bn ordinary profit), then the three tailwinds management itself names -- weak yen, record tungsten/gold/copper, the low-cost tungsten inventory release -- fade over FY2028-29 to the company's own FY2029 mid-cycle (ROE 8%, ROIC 7%, ordinary ~JPY105bn). The structural programme (Onahama smelter exit by Mar-2027, Sakai/Sambo integration, Johor strip exit, PPC company split, H.C. Starck tungsten recycling, Elemental USA e-scrap) removes the loss-makers and holds the mid-cycle EBITDA margin at ~7.8%, a touch under the ten-year average, while growth capex for secondary smelting stays above D&A. The axes: the metals price deck and JPY/USD; whether the FY2027-29 strategy is the first mid-term plan in a decade whose assumptions hold; and whether the resource-circulation pivot ever lifts ROIC above the 4-6% of FY2024-26.
scenario_narratives.bull: Copper stays in structural deficit on electrification and AI-datacentre demand, gold holds above $4,000, Chinese tungsten export controls keep APT elevated and the yen stays near 150-160. Smelting economics improve inside Pan Pacific Copper as Japanese primary capacity is cut, mine dividends (Los Pelambres, Mantoverde) compound at high copper, the tungsten/E-scrap recycling franchise earns the premium its scarcity implies, and management beats its FY2029 targets with ordinary profit sustained near JPY150bn (ROE ~12%). Deleveraging to net D/E 0.5x re-rates the equity from 0.7x book.
scenario_narratives.bear: FY2027 proves to be the peak: tungsten and gold roll over in H2, the yen firms, and FY2028-29 revert to the FY2024-25 band (ordinary JPY55-65bn, ROE ~5%). TC/RC stays at historic lows so the PPC stake earns little, the US/Europe secondary-smelter and recycling build-out keeps capex at 3.5% of revenue above D&A, and a further impairment cycle follows the Onahama one (FY2020 -72.9bn loss, FY2026 -20.4bn impairment). With JPY548bn of net debt against a JPY567bn market cap, a mid-cycle unlevered FCF of ~JPY45-50bn barely covers the debt at an 11x exit: the equity is close to worthless on this path and the out-of-the-money convertibles become the marginal financing.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 25%: net debt/EBITDA already at the 3.5x ceiling of the company's own target, a market cap roughly equal to net debt, a prior mid-term plan abandoned when its demand assumptions failed, and a decade in which company-defined FCF averaged ~JPY10bn a year. Bull cut from 35% to 25%: it requires copper, gold, tungsten and the yen to all stay favourable simultaneously plus execution of a multi-site restructuring. Base 50%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value the business on management's own mid-cycle, not on the record FY2027 the price-deck is delivering. The EBITDA line deliberately includes mine dividends and equity-method income (and therefore excludes the JPY302bn of investment securities from the bridge) because after the Pan Pacific Copper split an increasing share of the economics arrives as equity-method income. The terminal multiple is capped at 12x FCF for a sub-cost-of-capital-ROIC cyclical. Leverage is why the three scenarios are so far apart: JPY548bn of net debt is subtracted from every one of them.
key_risks_to_valuation: Peak-cycle base: if FY2027's JPY180bn ordinary profit proved to be the new normal rather than a peak, the base IV is far too low -- but management's own FY2029 targets (ROE 8%) say it is a peak.

The Pan Pacific Copper company split (~Feb 2027) will restate revenue and move smelting profit into equity-method income; later-year margins here are on a pre-split revenue base and must be re-based at the FY2028 update.
JPY70bn zero-coupon convertibles: ~13.5m shares (+10%) if the price clears JPY5,105-5,275; modelled as debt at today's price.

Working capital tracks metal prices: a further copper/gold leg up consumes cash even as profit rises (FY2027: -107bn guided), a reversal releases it; the -15% capture is a central estimate for a highly price-sensitive line.
Cash tax blend (23%) depends on the mix of exempt foreign dividends and equity-method income vs taxable domestic operating profit; a mix shift toward operating profit raises it toward 31%.
Gold-bullion lease/deposit book (net liability ~JPY325bn) is treated as operating, following the company's net-debt definition; a gold-price shock or counterparty issue would make it financial.
